One adverse claim-construction or trial outcome wipes out the bull case. Mode B: this is the dominant near-term risk and the MD&A liquidity discussion frames the cash position as if the franchise is durable.

rfm_tuples.R: We are substantially dependent on the commercial success of our only approved product, WAKIX. rfm_tuples.f: openFDA approved-drugs registry + self_text — verify single-product status and growth trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: openFDA confirms 1 application (NDA211150 WAKIX / pitolisant HCl), zero other approved Harmony products. FY2024 WAKIX revenue $714.7M = 100% of product revenue. FY2024 growth +22.8% YoY (vs $582.0M in 2023): 17.4% volume + 7% price - 3% rebates. Q1 2025: $184.7M vs Q1 2024 $154.6M = +19.5% (17% volume + 7% price - 4% rebates). Growth still strong but volume-growth rate is decelerating modestly and price/rebate spread is tightening (rebates 3% -> 4%). ~7,100 average patients on WAKIX in Q4 2024 vs estimated 165K diagnosed narcolepsy patients in US — ~4% penetration; runway exists but the narcolepsy market is mature and TAM-cap on single-indication WAKIX is finite.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honestly disclosed (PASS) but Mode B: ALL of the company's revenue, cash flow, and patent litigation exposure is one molecule for one indication (narcolepsy). The 2024 IH RTF removes a key TAM-expansion lever. The growth deceleration in Q1 + 4% rebate creep + narcolepsy market maturity together imply WAKIX is heading from +22% growth toward LSD/MSD growth before any generic launch hits. This single-product concentration is the dominant structural risk.

rfm_tuples.M_value: openFDA: WAKIX (pitolisant) is uniquely positioned as the only non-controlled narcolepsy product approved (other treatments listed in 10-K are all Schedule II/III/IV: Xyrem, Xywav, Sunosi, Provigil, Nuvigil, Lumryz, etc.). 10-K acknowledges Jazz's Lumryz (sodium oxybate ER, approved May 2023) and Avadel sodium-oxybate ER (Schedule III) as direct narcolepsy competitors. Centessa's ORX750 (orexin agonist, Phase 2) and Takeda TAK-861 (orexin agonist) noted as emerging competitors. Mode B nuance: the competitive landscape is shifting toward orexin agonists (Takeda, Centessa, Alkermes) where HRMY is several years behind, and Jazz's Lumryz is gaining share. The 'first-and-only non-scheduled' moat is real but not durable beyond 2027-2029 generic entry and emerging orexin class. Honest claim, but not a defensive moat for the full WAKIX life-cycle.

deterministic_flags.claim_drift_10k_to_10q: IH RTF disclosed in 10-K, omitted from Q1 2025 10-Q

summary: HRMY is a fundamentally solvent, profitable single-product specialty pharma (WAKIX / pitolisant for narcolepsy) with $489M cash, $178M debt, growing 19.5% in Q1 2025 and 22.8% in FY2024 against an unqualified Deloitte opinion. The framework's findings are mostly Mode B: (1) February 2025 FDA Refusal-to-File on the IH sNDA was disclosed in the 10-K but silently dropped from the Q1 2025 10-Q narrative, with IH repositioned from a 2026 to a 2028 PDUFA without being framed as a slip; (2) revenue + receivables are 100% concentrated in three specialty pharmacies (Caremark/Accredo/PANTHERx), with Caremark share climbing from 30% to 39% over two years; (3) the franchise faces six unresolved generic ANDA challengers (Lupin, Novitium, Zenara, AET, Annora, MSN) with a bench trial set for 2/17/2026, while Item 3 'no material pending claims' contradicts Note 13's 'could have a significant negative effect'; (4) executives sold ~$4.6M in 10b5-1-plan sales in the four months pre-cutoff with zero insider buying; (5) the pipeline is increasingly built via acquisitions (Zynerba 2023, Epygenix 2024, BP1.15205 sublicense 2024) with overlapping catalysts. Not lying — disclosures are largely there in the 10-K. But the company is single-product, single-indication, with one franchise drug under generic siege and the next-best growth indication (IH) just rejected by FDA. Honesty framework PASSES the issuer; structural risk is high. Verdict: NEUTRAL with mild SHORT-tilt on the trajectory.
